title: RAG source declaration
description: One document source (master plan 12.2, 4.5 check 3), one file per source under rag-sources/, listed in the manifest. AlixAI never crawls an entire machine, share or API: a source exists only if it is declared here with an explicit owner, scope, root, include/exclude rules, credential reference, size limits, refresh policy, deletion behaviour, parser policy, citation resolver, egress and retention. Every bullet of master plan 12.2 is a required property; optional properties are marked in their descriptions. The credential is only ever an opaque reference, never a secret. Authored as YAML; this schema validates the parsed JSON form.

id.description: The source ID, unique in the package and equal to the key the manifest lists this file under. It is the package-level name; the core mints its own src_ identifier per registered instance.

type.description: The source type (master plan 12.1). local_folder and mounted_volume: files on the host (the root kind must be folder or mount). application_document_api and http_api: documents or records from a scoped API (root kind api). exported_dataset: a read-only export in a folder or mount. documentation_package: versioned documentation shipped in the package (root kind package). The type fixes which root kinds are valid.

title.description: Optional human-readable name of the source, shown in citations when the source has no better display name.

description.description: Optional note on what the source contains.

languages.description: Optional. The languages the documents are written in; used for OCR and tokenisation hints. When absent the manifest languages apply.

owner.description: Who is accountable for the source. An ownerless source fails the audit.

scope.description: The application, tenant and workspace the source belongs to. Retrieval scope is applied before any text reaches a model.

root.description: The root folder, mount or API endpoint. Nothing outside the root is ever read.

include.description: The permitted path scope: globs relative to the root (for an API, request path patterns below the base). Only matching items are candidates. At least one: a source with no include rule matches nothing, which is not a declaration.

exclude.description: Globs that remove items from the included set. Exclusion wins over inclusion. May be empty.

query_scope.description: Optional, only for api roots: the permitted query scope. Without it only the root path and include patterns restrict an API source.

scope_params.description: Optional, only for api roots: extra scope parameters on list/fetch. Default (absent or all false) is today's behaviour: application_id, and tenant_id/workspace_id when those levels are not shared. The RAG index stays per tenant/workspace; when include_principal_id is true the host filters per user on every call. Do not mix principals' documents in one index without per-principal ACL at query time.

credential_ref.description: The credential reference held outside model context: an opaque cred: ID resolved from the OS secret store or an approved secret provider, or null when the source needs no credential. Never the secret itself.

formats.description: The accepted formats as concrete MIME types. The type is sniffed from content, not trusted from the file name. Anything else is skipped and counted. At least one.

limits.description: Size limits. All three are required: an unbounded source is not accepted.

deletion.description: What happens when an item or the whole source disappears.

parser.description: The parser and OCR policy. Parsing and OCR run in disposable sandboxed workers regardless of this policy.

citation.description: The citation and open-preview resolver: how a citation becomes a permission-checked reference the user can open.

egress.description: The network and egress permissions of the source.

retention.description: The retention and audit policy of the source's derived data.

egress_mode.description: Optional. What an external model provider may receive from this source, if the deployment enables external mode (external provider mode plan section 8). This is DATA egress, a different thing from `egress` above, which lists the network destinations the source may connect to. local_only (the default when the member is absent): content never leaves the deployment. allow_excerpt: bounded, authorised excerpts may be sent; it needs an explicit `classification` and is refused for a restricted source. allow_metadata: titles, IDs and status only, never content. deny: the source is excluded from the AlixAI capability entirely. A package can only restrict: the deployment, tenant and workspace policy decide whether anything leaves, and the most restrictive mode along that chain wins, so declaring allow_excerpt grants nothing by itself. Ignored while external mode is off.

classification.description: Optional. How sensitive the content of this source is: public, internal (the default when the member is absent), confidential or restricted. A restricted source never leaves the deployment.

name.description: The accountable person, team or role.

contact.description: Optional contact, preferably a role mailbox or team channel.

application_id.description: The application ID. Must equal application.id of the manifest.

tenant.description: How the source is bound to a tenant.

workspace.description: How the source is bound to a workspace. If the tenant binding is shared, so must this be: a source common to every tenant cannot belong to one workspace.

mode.description: request: the tenant (or workspace) of the verified request scope; the source definition serves every tenant and retrieval is always filtered to the caller's. fixed: exactly the tenant or workspace named in id. shared: visible across all tenants (or all workspaces of the tenant); an explicit opt-in for content that is not tenant-specific, such as public documentation.

id.description: The tenant or workspace ID. Required for fixed, not allowed otherwise.

root.description: The root, by kind. folder: an absolute path on the AlixAI host. mount: a mount registered by the operator, plus an optional sub-path. api: a manifest endpoint or an absolute http(s) URL. package: a folder shipped inside the package under documentation/.

path.description: Absolute path (POSIX, or a Windows drive path) with no '..' segment.

mount_id.description: The name of a mount the operator registered (HDD, SSD or NAS path visible to the host). The package never carries the host path of a mount.

path.description: Optional sub-path inside the mount, relative to the mount root, with the same path grammar as a package path.

endpoint.description: The ID of an mcp or openapi endpoint declared in the manifest. Exactly one of endpoint and url.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the API. Its host must have an entry in the egress allowlist the source references. Exactly one of endpoint and url.

base_path.description: Optional path prefix below the endpoint or URL; include patterns are relative to it.

include_principal_id.description: When true, every list and fetch request also carries the requesting principal id (parameter name principal_id, or principal_param when set) so the host can filter per user inside a tenant. Default false. The index remains per tenant/workspace; per-principal filtering then happens on the host for every call.

principal_param.description: Optional rename of the principal id query parameter. Default principal_id. Only used when include_principal_id is true.

allowed_parameters.description: The only query parameter names AlixAI may send. May be empty: no parameters at all.

fixed_parameters.description: Parameters always sent with a fixed value, for example a dataset or collection name. Their names must not also appear in allowed_parameters.

max_file_bytes.description: The largest single item accepted, in bytes, 1 to 2 GiB. Larger items are skipped and reported.

max_total_bytes.description: The most data the source may hold in total, in bytes, up to 1 TiB. Reaching it pauses ingestion and reports the source.

max_files.description: The most items the source may hold, 1 to 10 million.

method.description: poll: AlixAI rescans every interval_seconds. event: application events mark items changed; interval_seconds optionally adds a reconciliation scan. manual: only an operator-triggered sync runs; there is no interval.

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between scans, 60 to 31536000. Required for poll, optional for event, not allowed for manual.

event.description: For method event: the events endpoint and event type that signal a change. Required for event, not allowed otherwise.

endpoint.description: The ID of an events endpoint of the manifest.

event_type.description: A key of that endpoint's event_types.

purge_after_hours.description: When an item disappears from the source it is tombstoned and excluded from retrieval at once; its chunks, embeddings and cached answers are physically purged after this many hours, 0 to 8760. 0 purges immediately.

on_source_removed.description: What happens to derived data when the source declaration is removed or disabled. purge: tombstone everything and purge after purge_after_hours. disable: keep the derived data inert (never retrievable) until an operator purges it.

ocr.description: disabled: no OCR. when_no_text_layer: OCR only pages without extractable text. always: OCR every page.

ocr_languages.description: The languages OCR is run in. Required unless ocr is disabled, and not allowed when it is.

max_pages_per_file.description: Pages parsed per file, 1 to 10000; the rest are skipped and reported.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit for parsing one file, 1 to 600. A parse that times out marks the item failed, never half-indexed.

citation.description: The citation resolver, by kind. alixai_preview: AlixAI serves the permission-checked preview of the stored original. adapter_operation: the application resolves a citation to a preview through an adapter operation, reauthorizing the user. url_template: a link into the application on a fixed https host; the user's session at the application authorizes the open.

call.description: The adapter operation that returns the open or preview reference for an item.

url_template.description: An https URL with a fixed host and exactly one {item_id} placeholder in the path or query. The host cannot be templated.

entries.description: IDs of entries of the manifest's network.egress that this source may use. Empty means the source makes no network connection. Anything not listed is denied.

derived_data_days.description: How long derived data (chunks, embeddings, indexes) is kept, 1 to 3650 days, or null to keep it for as long as the source item exists. Derived data can always be rebuilt from the source.

import_originals.description: false: originals stay owned by their provider and are read in place. true: AlixAI keeps an imported copy so previews survive a deleted original; the copy follows the deletion policy.

audit.description: The audit policy for access to the source.

record_access.description: true: every retrieval from the source and every citation open is written to the audit log.

retention_days.description: How long those audit events are kept, 1 to 3650.
